newsitem.title: INDIA: India federal police ordered to arrest politician.
newsitem.headline: India federal police ordered to arrest politician.

text.p: The head of India's federal police agency on Tuesday ordered officials in the eastern state of Bihar to execute an arrest warrant against former chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, official sources said.

Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Director R.C. Sharma ordered officials in the Bihar state capital of Patna to execute the non-bailable warrants against Yadav and three other politicians involved in a $280 million farm funds scandal, the sources said.

The CBI order was issued shortly after the nation's Supreme Court rejected an appeal by Yadav against a state court's order refusing to grant him "anticipatory bail", allowed under Indian law to people expecting possible arrest.

Yadav was forced to resign last Friday after a special court in the Bihar state capital of Patna issued arrest warrants against him and three other politicians in the $280 million scandal involving alleged embezzlement of animal welfare funds.
Yadav's stubborn refusal to quit his post after the CBI indicted him in the scandal in April had triggered a crisis in India's ruling United Front coalition.

The 15-party United Front alliance decided on Friday not to admit Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) group into its fold, but Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has been widely criticised for not acting to remove Yadav from office earlier.
